entryPoint: SLA::priorityEscalation() — include/class.sla.php lines 116-118. A zero-argument instance method on the SLA ORM model (extends VerySimpleModel) that reports the priority-escalation flag state for `$this` SLA plan. Current body: `return $this->flags && self::FLAG_ESCALATE;`
coreLogic: The entire core logic is the single expression `$this->flags && self::FLAG_ESCALATE` where FLAG_ESCALATE = 0x0002 (a class const shared with FLAG_ACTIVE=0x0001, FLAG_NOALERTS=0x0004, FLAG_TRANSIENT=0x0008). This uses PHP's logical && (not the bitwise & used by every sibling flag-check in the same class: isActive() uses `$this->flags & self::FLAG_ACTIVE`, isTransient() uses `$this->flags & self::FLAG_TRANSIENT`, sendAlerts() uses `0 === ($this->flags & self::FLAG_NOALERTS)`, and getInfo() itself computes `$this->flags & self::FLAG_ESCALATE`). Because FLAG_ESCALATE (2) is a non-zero literal, it is always truthy in a boolean context, so `&& self::FLAG_ESCALATE` is a no-op and the expression is functionally equivalent to `(bool)$this->flags`. This is a pre-existing bug in the live code: priorityEscalation() actually returns true whenever ANY bit is set in flags (e.g. FLAG_ACTIVE alone, with escalation NOT requested), and only returns false when flags is exactly 0. This buggy behavior — not the bitwise-correct behavior implied by getInfo()/sla.yaml — is what callers see today and is what must be preserved by extraction.
consumers: No call sites found anywhere in the codebase for SLA::priorityEscalation() itself (grep across include/, scp/, api/, include/plugins/ matched only the method's own definition) — it is currently dead/unused code, not wired into include/class.ticket.php's overdue/escalation flow despite include/i18n/en_US/sla.yaml documenting FLAG_ESCALATE as intended to 'cause the ticket priority to be escalated when it is marked overdue'.

Related (but distinct) exposure path 1: SLA::getInfo() (include/class.sla.php:73-80) computes `$base['enable_priority_escalation'] = $this->flags & self::FLAG_ESCALATE` (correct bitwise, NOT the same code path as priorityEscalation()) and is called from include/staff/slaplan.inc.php:8 (`$info=$sla->getInfo();`) to populate the SLA-plan edit form's $info array for display only.

Related exposure path 2: SLA::update($vars, &$errors) (include/class.sla.php:155-212) persists `$vars['enable_priority_escalation']` directly into `$this->flags` via bitwise OR at line 191 (no isset()/ternary normalization, unlike disable_overdue_alerts/transient at lines 174-175). Called from scp/slas.php line 30 (update action) and line 41 (add action) with `$vars = $_POST`. The SLA-plan admin form template (include/staff/slaplan.inc.php) has no HTML input field named 'enable_priority_escalation', so $_POST never actually contains that key on UI saves — every save via scp/slas.php therefore ORs in null/0, always clearing FLAG_ESCALATE. This is a facade-level quirk in update()/the form, outside the extraction target, documented only because the ticket asks how getInfo()/update() expose and persist the flag.
inputShape: None — priorityEscalation() takes zero parameters. It reads only `$this->flags`, an int column on the SLA_TABLE row already hydrated into the SLA instance by VerySimpleModel (either via DB lookup/fetch, or via `new SLA(array('flags'=>$n))` which sets properties in memory with no DB query).
outputShape: Returns a plain PHP boolean (the result of the && operator, which is always type bool). CURRENT ACTUAL contract (bug-included, must be preserved): true iff `$this->flags` is non-zero (i.e. any of FLAG_ACTIVE/FLAG_ESCALATE/FLAG_NOALERTS/FLAG_TRANSIENT is set); false iff `$this->flags === 0`. This differs from the INTENDED/documented contract (matching getInfo()'s bitwise field and sla.yaml) of: true iff bit 0x0002 (FLAG_ESCALATE) specifically is set, false otherwise. No mutation of $this or any argument; pure read, new boolean value returned, nothing passed by reference.
sideEffects: None within priorityEscalation() itself: it performs a pure read of the already in-memory `$this->flags` property. No DB query is triggered by this call — VerySimpleModel hydrates the full row (including flags) when the SLA object is constructed/looked up, before priorityEscalation() is ever invoked.
No global state ($cfg, etc.) is read or written by priorityEscalation().
No lazy-loading, caching, or file I/O occurs in priorityEscalation().

Out-of-scope context only (facade-adjacent, NOT part of what gets extracted): SLA::update() — the surrounding facade method that also touches this bit — calls $this->save() (DB write via parent::save(), sets $this->updated = SqlFunction::NOW() when dirty) and fires Signal::send('object.edited', $this, ...) for isactive/disable_overdue_alerts/transient changes specifically (flagChanged() is never invoked for FLAG_ESCALATE, so no audit signal fires today when the escalation bit changes via update()).
constraints: Lift the exact current expression `$this->flags && self::FLAG_ESCALATE` verbatim into the extracted service — do NOT silently correct it to bitwise `&`. The extraction must reproduce the existing bug (truthy whenever flags != 0) for parity; fixing the bug is out of scope for a strangler extraction.

flags=0 is the only input where the buggy (&&) and intended (&) semantics agree (both false) — this is the required edge case per the acceptance criteria and must be captured explicitly in the parity harness.

Zero-argument method; no by-reference parameters; return value must remain directly usable in boolean contexts (`if ($sla->priorityEscalation())`) exactly as today, even though PHP enforces no declared return type here.

Do not modify getInfo() or update() — they are separate, already bitwise-correct (for getInfo()) or independently-behaved (for update()) call paths that read/write the same underlying flags bit but are not the facade entry point named in this seam; only priorityEscalation() is patched.
The extracted service must reference SLA::FLAG_ESCALATE (or receive the flags int as its only input) rather than hardcoding the literal 2, so it stays correct if flag bit values are ever renumbered.
No new DB reads/writes may be introduced — the flags value must be passed in already-hydrated, exactly as `$this->flags` is read today, with no re-fetch.

Per the anti-recursion rule, the extracted service must never call back into SLA::priorityEscalation() — it should either take the raw flags int (lifted-logic pattern) or take the SLA/flags value as a parameter and return the lifted boolean expression directly.
harnessInputShape: JSON object with a single field: `flags` (int) — the raw SLA.flags bitmask value to test on an in-memory SLA instance (constructed via `new SLA(array('flags' => $input['flags']))`, which sets the property with no DB query). The harness calls `->priorityEscalation()` on that instance and echoes {input, output} where output is the raw (current, bug-included) boolean result. Suggested cases per acceptance criteria: flags=2 (FLAG_ESCALATE only — escalation enabled), flags=3 (FLAG_ACTIVE|FLAG_ESCALATE — escalation enabled, also active), flags=1 (FLAG_ACTIVE only, no ESCALATE bit — escalation 'disabled' per intended semantics, but returns true today due to the && bug), and flags=0 (the edge case — the only input where buggy and intended semantics agree, both false).
